frozen_candidate_root_contribution: The root contributes the notion of bringing a matter to a FIRM, AUTHORITATIVE, DECISIVE settlement — fixing/binding something soundly so that it holds and rival options or corruption are barred. The residue is not "knowledge" and not "separation"; it is the act/quality/faculty/agency of decisive determination that makes a thing firm and settled.

internal_discovery.candidate_root_contribution: The root contributes the notion of bringing a matter to a FIRM, AUTHORITATIVE, DECISIVE settlement — fixing/binding something soundly so that it holds and rival options or corruption are barred. The residue is not "knowledge" and not "separation"; it is the act/quality/faculty/agency of decisive determination that makes a thing firm and settled.
internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Across all 210 confirmed occurrences the root's steady contribution is "decisive, firm, authoritative settling of a matter." Surface variety is carried by FORM and CONSTRUCTION, not by the root: (1) Form I verb yaHkumu / iHkum = to render the settlement, overwhelmingly with the construction bayna-hum ("judge/decide BETWEEN" disputants) or bi-... ("decide BY/WITH" a norm: bi-l-Haqq, bi-l-qisT, bi-maa anzala llaah) — e.g. 5:42, 5:48, 4:105, 38:26, 2:213, 16:124, 39:3, 22:69; (2) taHkumuun "how do you decide/determine?" carries the same act, usually in rebuke of arbitrary determinations (37:154; 68:36; saaʔa maa yaHkumuun 16:59, 29:4, 45:21, 6:136); (3) Form II Hakkama = CAUSE someone to be the decider, "make you arbiter" (4:65; 5:43); (4) Form VI yataHaakamuu = mutually SEEK a decider's settlement (4:60, to Taghut); (5) Form IV (uHkimat 11:1; yuHkimu 22:52) and participle muHkam(aat/-ah) (3:7; 47:20) = render/made FIRM, decisive, unambiguous — the clearest internal anchor of the "firm-fixing" residue, since muHkamaat stand opposed to mutashaabihaat; (6) noun Hukm = the binding determination/authority itself ("the Hukm belongs to God alone" 12:40, 12:67, 6:57, 40:12; "to Him belongs the Hukm" 28:70, 28:88, 6:62); (7) Hukm as a God-given endowment of sound decisive discernment to prophets (12:22, 21:74, 21:79, 26:83, 19:12, 3:79, 6:89, 45:16); (8) Hikma "wisdom" = the FACULTY that yields sound firm determinations, taught alongside the Book (2:129, 2:151, 3:48, 62:2, 2:269, 16:125, 31:12); (9) agent nouns Hakam "arbiter" (6:114, 4:35), Hukkaam "rulers/judges" (2:188), Haakimiin / khayr al-Haakimiin / aHkam al-Haakimiin "deciders / best-and-most-decisive of deciders" (7:87, 10:109, 11:45, 95:8); (10) adjective Hakiim "all-wise / firmly-decreeing," as a divine epithet (usually paired ʕaziiz Hakiim, ʕaliim Hakiim) and of the Book (al-kitaab al-Hakiim 10:1, 31:2; al-qurʔaan al-Hakiim 36:2) and of "a decisively-decreed matter" (amr Hakiim 44:4). Subtract form and construction and the same core remains everywhere: decisive, firm, authoritative determination.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: FORM layer: I = perform the determination (judge); II Hakkama = causative "appoint/treat as the decider"; IV aHkama/yuHkimu + participle muHkam = factitive "make firm/decisive/unambiguous"; VI taHaakama = reciprocal "seek adjudication from an arbiter." CONSTRUCTION layer: Hakama bayna X = adjudicate a dispute between parties; Hakama bi-Y = decide by/according to a norm (bi-l-Haqq, bi-l-qisT, bi-l-ʕadl, bi-maa anzala llaah); lam yaHkum bi-maa anzala llaah = fail to rule by the revealed norm. NOMINAL layer: Hukm = the act/authority of determination (masdar + authority); Hikma = the nominalized FACULTY (fiʕla pattern) that produces sound determinations; Hakam/Hukkaam/Haakim(iin) = agent nouns; aHkam = elative "most decisive/sound"; Hakiim = intensive adjective/epithet. PARTICIPANTS: God as supreme/best determiner; prophets/judges as endowed determiners; humans criticized for arbitrary or misplaced determination. After stripping all of the above, the non-empty residue is: firm, authoritative, decisive settling that fixes a matter and closes off alternatives.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: The largest strain is the Hikma "wisdom" cluster and the fixed epithet Hakiim. In 16:125 (adʕu ... bi-l-Hikma wa-l-mawʕiZa l-Hasana), 2:151 / 3:48 / 62:2 / 5:110 (teaching "the Book and al-Hikma"), and 2:269 (yuʔti l-Hikmata man yashaaʔ), "wisdom" surfaces as a taught content or manner of address, where no overt act of adjudication is present — the decisive-determination residue survives only as the underlying FACULTY of sound firm discernment, an agentive/metonymic extension of the bare act. Likewise the 84 Hakiim tokens as a near-formulaic divine epithet (ʕaziiz Hakiim, ʕaliim Hakiim) could, taken alone, be read as generic "wise." These are reconciled — not forced — because the same corpus internally fixes Hakiim to the decisive-firm sense via amr Hakiim (44:4, "a decisively-decreed matter") and via the muHkamaat/muHkama firmness cluster (3:7; 47:20; 11:1; 22:52), and because Hakiim is repeatedly held DISTINCT from knowledge by pairing (Hakiim + ʕaliim, Hakiim + khabiir), so its own contribution cannot collapse into "knowing."
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: The main rival reading assigns the root two only loosely related cores — (a) "judge/rule/authority" for the verb + Hukm + agent nouns, and (b) "wisdom/soundness" for Hikma + the Hakiim epithet — treating the link as historical polysemy rather than one live residue, so that "wise" in ʕaziiz Hakiim carries knowledge-quality content with no decisive-fixing element. A second rival narrows the residue to "authoritative decision/verdict," which fits the verbal and Hukm clusters cleanly but must strain to cover muHkam "firmly-made/unambiguous" (which is about firmness of construction, not verdict) and Hikma (faculty). The proposed unifying residue — "firm decisive fixing of a matter" — is preferred because it is the one description that natively covers BOTH the verdict sense AND the muHkam firmness sense AND the wisdom-faculty sense, and it is anchored internally by amr Hakiim and the muHkamaat/mutashaabihaat contrast rather than imported from lexicon.
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: The residue is distinctive against nearest roots and this is testable inside the packet. vs q-D-y (qaDaa, "decree/carry out/complete"): 4:65 places qaDayta and Hakkama in one verse — the arbiter is MADE to determine (Hkm), then His decision (qaDaa) is what they must accept, so Hkm = the binding determining, distinct. vs f-S-l ("separate/distinguish/decide by parting"): 6:57 juxtaposes "the Hukm belongs only to God" with "He is the best of faaSiliin (separators)" — Hukm (firm binding settlement) is kept lexically apart from faSl (cutting apart), and 11:1 pairs uHkimat (made firm) with then fuSSilat (then set out in detail). vs ʕ-l-m (knowledge): the recurrent ʕaliim Hakiim / Hakiim ʕaliim pairings force Hakiim to contribute something OTHER than knowing — namely sound firm determination. So the residue is non-empty, falsifiable (it would fail on any token meaning purely "know," "separate," or "have mercy" with no firm-determination content), and no such token occurs.
unresolved_cases: Hikma-as-taught-content / manner: 16:125, 2:129, 2:151, 3:48, 4:54, 5:110, 62:2, 2:231, 33:34, 43:63 — reconciled only via the FACULTY (sound-firm-determination) extension, not the bare adjudicative act; flagged as the softest zone of the residue.

Formulaic divine epithet Hakiim (bulk of the 84 ADJ tokens, e.g. ʕaziiz Hakiim / ʕaliim Hakiim in 2:209, 2:220, 2:228, 4:11, 4:158, 9:x, 57:1, 59:24 …) — reconciled to 'firmly/soundly decreeing' via amr Hakiim (44:4) and the muHkam cluster, but read in isolation it admits a bleached 'wise' sense; this is the point of maximum reliance on cross-token anchoring rather than local context.
internal_discovery.rationale: All 210 occurrences were individually assessed and every one is reconcilable to a single non-empty residue — "firm, authoritative, decisive determination that fixes a matter and bars alternatives" — once FORM (I judge / II appoint-as-judge / IV+participle make-firm / VI seek-adjudication), CONSTRUCTION (bayna = between disputants; bi- = by a norm), and the noun-of-act vs noun-of-faculty vs agent-noun vs epithet distinctions are subtracted. No occurrence requires a meaning with zero firm-determination content, so root unity holds without appeal to a majority and without a hard counterexample; hence PREFERRED, not UNRESOLVED. Strength is MODERATE rather than STRONG for two honest reasons: (1) the large Hikma cluster and the formulaic Hakiim epithet are reconciled through a metonymic FACULTY/agentive extension of the core act and, taken in isolation, admit a competing bleached "wisdom/knowledge" reading; (2) the strongest internal proof that Hakiim keeps the decisive-firm residue (amr Hakiim 44:4; the muHkamaat contrast in 3:7; uHkimat 11:1; yuHkimu 22:52) is cross-token anchoring rather than local evidence at each epithet token. The residue is nonetheless distinctive (held apart from qaDaa, faSl, and ʕilm within the packet itself) and falsifiable, so the judgment is a positive but appropriately hedged PREFERRED/MODERATE. Nothing here is canonical; evidence is confined to the cited verse occurrences.

adversarial_verification.notes: Adversarial refutation attempt over all 210 occurrences (full coverage) failed to find any occurrence where the proposed residue is absent after subtracting form/construction/context. All clusters reconcile: (1) V 'judge between' (4:105, 5:42/48/49, 38:22/26, 21:78, 22:56/69, 24:48/51, 2:213, 4:58, 60:10) = decisive authoritative settlement of disputes; (2) V polemical (16:59, 29:4, 45:21, 6:136, 37:154, 68:36/39, 10:35) = the ACT/faculty of reaching a settled verdict, present regardless of the verdict's (condemned) content; (3) V(II)/V(VI) ḥakkama/taḥākama (4:65, 5:43, 4:60) = agency of arbitration; (4) N ḥukm authority/decree (12:40/67, 6:57/62, 13:41, 28:70/88, 40:12, 42:10) with 13:41 'no one reverses His ḥukm' vividly showing firm/settled; (5) N ḥukm prophetic faculty (12:22, 19:12, 21:74/79, 26:21, 28:14, 3:79, 6:89, 45:16); (6) N ḥakam/ḥukkām arbiter (6:114, 4:35, 2:188); (7) ḥākimīn (10:109, 11:45, 12:80, 7:87, 95:8); (8) muḥkam/uḥkimat/yuḥkimu 'made firm' (3:7, 47:20, 11:1, 22:52) = purest 'firm/fixed'; (9) ADJ ḥakīm epithet (~84x) = one whose determinations are firm/decisive, consistently paired-but-distinct with ʿAlīm/ʿAzīz/Khabīr. Distinctiveness holds: packet separates ḥkm from ʿilm (ḥukm/ʿilm, ḥakīm/ʿalīm) and from separation (6:57 al-ḥukm vs khayr al-fāṣilīn); residue is neither knowledge nor separation. Weakest/stretch zone is the ḥikmah 'wisdom' cluster (kitāb wa-ḥikmah formula; 2:269; 16:125 daʿwah bi-l-ḥikmah), reconciled only under the 'faculty of firm sound judgment' reading — but 38:20 pairs ḥikmah with faṣl al-khiṭāb (decisive speech) and the packet's ʿilm-pairings preserve distinctiveness, so it reconciles rather than fails. Honest adversarial conclusion: universal presence holds; no unreconciled occurrence found. Caveat: residue is broad; its falsifiability rests mainly on the explicit exclusion of 'knowledge' and 'separation', which the packet's own contrastive pairings uphold.
